articles.title: Carrick brushes off Martínez’s failure to apologise publicly to United director Wilcox
articles.summary: Manchester United coach accepts defender’s apology. ‘He’s realised he’s made a mistake and that’s enough’ Michael Carrick brushed off Lisandro Martínez not offering Jason Wilcox a public apology after the defender criticised Manchester United’s director of football in the wake of Tuesday’s defeat…
body: Martínez referred directly to Wilcox after the 2-0 Champions League loss, saying: “I expect more from our technical director.”

On Thursday Martínez issued an apology that did not mention Wilcox or withdraw the essence of his outburst: the need for more squad investment. “The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise,” he said.

Carrick was asked whether he respected Martínez for not saying sorry to Wilcox. “He’s released his statement, he’s realised he’s made a mistake and that’s enough for all of us to move on with,” United’s manager said.

Carrick was pressed on whether it would have been better if Martínez had apologised to Wilcox and for his wider comments about investment, rather than just saying sorry for the timing and location of his interview. “From our point of view, the acknowledgment of what’s been done has certainly been enough, we’ve moved on and we’re definitely not looking back at it now,” he replied.

articles.title: Police investigating antisemitic Nazi chants from Hajduk Split fans
articles.summary: Footage shows Hajduk supporters chanting outside the stadium about Auschwitz and Adolf Hitler before their Conference League match against Ajax.
body: Croatian police are investigating antisemitic chanting by Hajduk Split fans which took place before their Conference League game against Ajax on Thursday.
Footage published online shows Hajduk supporters chanting outside the stadium about Auschwitz and in support of Adolf Hitler.
A large supporters' march to the stadium was led by a yellow car carrying a coffin marked "Ajax" on its roof.
Croatia's ombudswoman Tena Simonovic Einwalter, an independent official appointed by parliament to safeguard human rights, called the incident a "manifestation of hatred and intolerance".

articles.title: Mikel Arteta defends job cuts at Arsenal to help club ‘evolve and create success’
articles.summary: Up to 60 roles at risk after cost-cutting review. Arteta signed new deal worth more than £20m a season. Mikel Arteta has defended Arsenal’s decision to cut up to 60 jobs and insisted it was necessary to ensure they can continue achieving success.
body: The Premier League champions are understood to have informed some, but not all, of the staff whose positions are at risk after a consultation process started by Boston Consulting Group (BCG) before the end of last season. Arsenal hope the number of redundancies can be reduced and will attempt to redeploy affected employees wherever possible, although some job losses may be unavoidable.

It is understood the catering and travel departments are among the affected, and that the men’s and women’s first-team performance and coaching staff will not be impacted. The academy, Arsenal Women, Arsenal in the Community, the Arsenal Foundation and site security teams are also exempt, although other areas of the wider football operation are included in the review, which was overseen internally by the managing director, Richard Garlick.

The timing of the proposed cuts has attracted scrutiny after last week’s announcement of Arteta’s new contract, worth more than £20m a season. Arsenal say the restructuring process began before the deal was announced and the manager said he was not the appropriate person to answer questions about the redundancies.

articles.title: Denver Broncos & Minnesota Vikings prove that it’s better to be lucky than good
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings and Denver Broncos are two very opposite NFL teams, yet they are both finding ways to win games that most teams don’t. The Vikings can’t control the ball offensively but are undefeated. The Broncos are continuing their philosophy from last year by winning one-score games.
body: The Broncos won 11 games last season by 8 points or fewer. This year, they have won every game by the same margin. Their offense is putting up less than 20 points per game and is last in the league in yards per play (4.4).

How does this team continue to find ways to win games with poor QB play? Defensively, they are holding their opponents to the 9th-fewest points per game (20.8). Their defense is carrying the load, as they are ranked 3rd in EPA/Pass.

Bo Nix hasn’t looked like himself this season. He suffered an injury last year in the playoffs that put him out for the rest of the postseason. The numbers are not good. Their offense against Seattle struggled, while the defense was able to force Sam Darnold to throw two interceptions.
An interesting stat for Bo Nix is 2026: Bo Nix ranks 701st out of 701 in average pass length (4.9 air yards per attempt) over the past 20 years.

articles.title: The All Blacks' Haka explained - plus rugby's other rituals
articles.summary: One of the most intriguing and anticipated moments in the sport of rugby union: the sight of New Zealand's All Blacks performing their world-famous haka as the opposition stands before them.
body: But how much do you know about the haka? And also of the three other ceremonial war dances which take place in rugby: the Cibi, Siva Tau and Sipi Tau.

An ancient traditional Māori practice, there is no single recorded date for the haka's first-ever performance owing to this very reason. It has been practised by indigenous Māori communities for centuries.
The earliest point at which Europeans witnessed the haka was the 18th century: Joseph Banks and James Cook on their first voyage to New Zealand in 1769 recorded the haka as "vigorous and ferocious".

In terms of its introduction into sport, New Zealand's first rugby union side visited Australia in Sydney in 1884 and performed the haka. During 1888/89, a 'New Zealand native team' toured the UK for the first time, performing the haka on October 3 1888 against Surrey in a tour match.

articles.title: 'One of the best weeks of my life' - Kartal feeling fresh ahead of Wuhan semi-finals
articles.summary: British star Sonay Kartal says she is due a couple of new tattoos after enjoying "one of the best weeks" of her life by reaching the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open.
body: Kartal claimed one of the biggest wins of the career as she beat world No 6 Elina Svitolina on Friday.
The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, seized her first match-point opportunity to complete another stunning victory.
Kartal, who made her breakthrough by reaching the fourth round of last year's Wimbledon, advanced to the last four of a WTA 1000 event for the first time.
"Definitely one of the best weeks of my life," she said. "You could say, results-wise, that is definitely the best for me so far.
